title: Onboard eos-13b-v1.0: metadata, perf profiles, and changelog automation
author: Samir Patel
description:
Onboard eos-13b-v1.0 into the model registry with metadata, curated performance profiles, and updates to changelog/release-note generation so new model entries are automatically surfaced in release artifacts. Motivation: Eos 13B is a high-throughput open model that showed strong cost/latency tradeoffs for our small- and medium-sequence workloads during benchmarking (see linked Linear item ENG-4421). This PR performs three coordinated changes: 1) add canonical metadata for eos-13b-v1.0 (authors, licenses, tokenizer, model family, supported precisions), 2) add performance profiles for common serving modes (hosted, dedicated with batching, and quantized int8 paths) with measured p50/p95/p99 latencies and per-token cost estimates, and 3) integrate the new model metadata into changelog/release-note automation templates so onboarding events generate a draft release note and changelog entry automatically. Checklist:
- [x] Add metadata YAML and model alias mapping
- [x] Add perf profile JSONs and human-readable summary for console
- [x] Add unit/integration tests for registry validation
- [x] Wire model metadata into changelog-generator templates
- [x] Update docs snippet and example for model versioning
Testing and validation: I ran the perf harness (perf-canary subset) against a dedicated test cluster to produce the profile numbers and validated formatting against the changelog generator locally. CI passed full unit tests and the model-registry linting rules. Backwards compatibility: metadata keys are additive and follow existing schema; no breaking changes expected. Rollout: merged to main; the changelog automation will pick up the new entry on next release cycle. Notes for reviewers: see inline comments about quantization buckets and fallback model variants for low-memory hosts.
